HPV/ Oral Cancer

By: Michael Duffett | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
It's not in the South African media but surgeons here are increasingly operating on patients with throat cancer caused by the HPV virus and not smoking, alcohol or bad diet. International literature is suggesting that HPV will overtake smoking as a leading cause of oropharyngeal cancers. The reason it seems that oral sex is the cause and more men are prone to it because of their sexual practice of cunninglingus. In fact these increases are seen more in developed countries than undeveloped countries. A controversial aspect of this story is the following - whether a patient has throat cancer from HPV or not does not affect treatment which is either surgery or radiation. This is why national labs are not testing for the virus and so we have no idea the extent to which HPV throat cancers are prevalent in South Africa. However we will be honing in on a medical practice and a particular doctor who regularly performs surgery on patients with throat cancer caused by the HPV virus. This private practice unlike other private practices always request private labs to test for HPV.

Those with HPV are informed because the prognosis is better than cancers non-HPV related. The program will address the need for safety precautions. We will cover the fact that school children a re being vaccinated and we will get a doctor to talk about the need for safer sex. He admits this is a pipe dream because many practice risky sex. He will advocate that all sexually active men and woman should be vaccinated which can delay the onset of HPV. In this program John Webb can hold up a "dam" which is a piece of cloth which needs to be placed over the vagina to effect safer cunninglingus. The point is that it is doubtful that people will go to this lengths but we need to put it out there.

The take home message is that HPV related throat cancers are on the rise and there are even some reports that say that it could overtake cervical cancer in the years ahead in terms of deaths. That is scary.

We really like the story – we are not clear on:
• Why people between 9 and 26 are the most viable – and whether you should have it after you become sexually active? Please clarify what these age limits mean and why these are the limits. Please make it crystal clear what you mean?
• We want to know how men would know that they are a carrier of the HP virus? We want to know how you would know and clarify exactly how you would be tested? And if you are a carrier then what do you do?

Press Release:


HPV and Oral Sex
Traditionally oropharyngeal cancers were directly linked to smoking. However, over the past few years specialists have seen a rise in these cancers across the developed world. The leading cause? The human papillomavirus, a sexually transmitted disease passed on through oral sex. Carte Blanche speaks to a top Johannesburg physician, whose practice has seen about 50 oropharyngeal cancers, half of them caused by HPV.


Script:


HPV OROPHARYNGEAL CANCER SCRIPT

It is one of the most commonly sexually transmitted diseases in the world with up to 80 percent of sexually active people contracting it at some point in their lives. - HPV or human papillomavirus – and it is the biggest single cause of cervical cancer in South Africa. Now its has been linked to cancers in other parts of the body such the oropharynx. Dr Mark Torres-Holmes who operates at Mediclinic in Morningside is seeing first hand the rise of these cancers.

Dr Torres-Holmes: About 50% of the cancers that we see that are in the oropharynx are now HPV related.

The oropharynx consists of the base of the tongue, the tonsils and the soft pallet.

LINK (JOHN WEBB): SMOKING AND ALCOHOL ARE GENERALLY SEEN AS THE TWO MAIN RISK FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH OROPHARYNGEAL CANCERS, BUT EXPERTS PREDICT THAT IN THE DEVELOPED WORLD THOSE TWO WILL SOON BE OVERTAKEN BY HPV WHICH IS TRADITIONALLY ASSOCIATED WITH CERVICAL CANCER.

HPV is passed on though intimate skin-to-skin contact and most people are not even aware they are affected as they are asymptomatic and their immune system clears the virus within two years. Most genital hpv strains are low risk but can lead to warts. Some strains are high risk as they can lead to cancer of the genitals, anus and increasingly the oropharynx. In the USA there are about 50 000 new cases of oropharyngeal cancers each year and its believed that 70 % of these are associated with hpv.

the specialised Head and Neck Clinic in which Dr Torres-Holmes works has seen about 50 such cases in the last two years. He’s concerned that about half of them are hpv related.

John: That is a pretty scary statistic isn’t it? I mean you say at least half, possibly more than that?
Dr. Torres-Holmes: What's even quite scary is the fact that it is the one cancer that’s on the rise so we are really seeing a problem.

LINK: SO HOW DID RESEARCHERS AND SCIENTISTS DISCOVER THE LINK BETWEEN HPV AND OROPHARYNGEAL CANCERS? WELL MASS CAMPAIGNS OVER THE PAST FEW DECADES HAVE SEEN A DECREASE IN SMOKING AND YET THESE CANCERS ARE ON THE INCREASE.

It was cervical cancer, according to Professor Vikash Sewram , which provided the answer.

Prof Sewram: What was found in the US is that there was still an increase in oropharyngeal cancers in non smokers and that is where the idea of looking at other infectious agents and given the association of HPV with cervical cancer and due to sexual contact it was then hypothesized that HPV could be related to oropharyngeal cancers.

And oropharyngeal cancer was thrust into the spot light in 2013 when actor Michael Douglas claimed that his throat cancer was due to hpv and oral sex. .

Its believed that those who have had many oral sex partners are most at risk. However it can take a number of years for a cancerous tumor to develop in the oropharynx.

Dr Kevin Rebe is not surprised at the rise of these caners.

Dr. Rebe: I think that looking at the sexual world we know that there are more opportunities for sex, the social media realm has created that for us. We certainly know from many studies that people are starting to have sex at earlier ages. We know that increased number of partners are a factor in many peoples lives. So I think there are a number of things that we can identify that could conceivably be raising the amount of sexual encounters and therefore the amount of HPV transference.

The latest statistics available in South Africa is the 2011 report from the national cancer registry which lists 355 new cases of orogphanbgeal cancer. However clinicians believe its vastly underreported.


LINK: PART OF THE CHALLENGE WHEN TRYING TO ESTABLISH THE LINK BETWEEN OROPHARYNGEAL CANCERS AND HPV IS THAT NEITHER THE NATIONAL NOR THE PRIVATE PATHOLOGY LABS ARE ROUTINTELY TESTING FOR THE VIRUS

And this was confirmed by a number of private laboratories we contacted.

John: Am I right in saying that not all doctors specify HPV screening?
Dr. Nayler: It is only a specific subset of doctors. Those that are attending the multidisciplinary clinic where we have taken a decision that all oral cancers should be tested for HPV but some other doctors certainly don’t request it.

That’s because an hpv positive result does not necessarily, at this stage, dictate the type of treatment offered to patients but it does affect prognosis. It’s for this reason that Dr Torres-Holmes sends all his oropharyngeal specimens for HPV testing.

Dr. Torres-Holmes: We have found that patients who are HPV positive do better. Prognostically they do better and this is the main reason we are testing for it at the moment is we can guide and inform our patients before treatment begins regarding how well we think they are going to do.

And they do better according to Dr. Julie Wetter, if the patient is a non-smoker.

John: Doctor you mention that oropharyngeal cancers caused by HPV have a better prognosis, why is that?
Dr. Wetter: Well just by having a tumor that was caused by HPV you have a different; you obviously have a different type of cancer from one that was caused by smoking. It once again comes down to the genetics probably in that these are two different tumors. They have many similarities but they are, the drivers to the mutations that cause them to occur in the first place are slightly different.

Oropharyngeal cancers can be very devastating. Treatment options are either surgery, or radio or chemotherapy or a combination.

Dr. Torres-Holmes: I would say for oropharynx, particularly HPV cancers, they respond so well to radiation often with chemotherapy that is the vast majority of the time the treatment we suggest.

Several months of grueling radio and chemotherapy are sometimes indicated,

Dr. Wetter: It takes at least I would say two months to recover from that. So it is half a year out of somebodies life before they even starting to feel as though they are semi functional.

Patients whose oropharyngeal cancer is linked to HPV have an 80% 5 year survival rate. For those cancers not caused by HPV, it’s 50% 5 years survival rate.
LINK: IF WE ARE GOING TO SEE A SURGE IN OROPHARYNGEALCANCER, THE QUESITON BECOMES WHAT CAN WE DO TO PROTECT OURSELVES AGAINST THIS VIRUS?

A vaccination which wards off high risk trains of hpv is available for both sexes. It’s recommended that the vaccine is received before a person becomes sexually active. A national roll out plan is now taking place in South Africa where girls aged 9 till 11 are being vaccinated. Safe sex is always advocated, as is now safer oral sex, which includes the use of maee and female condoms.

Dr. Rebe: So the reality is that people are not using them. What we need to be looking at is are there other ways that we could make the sex they have responsible that allows them to make a valid choice about whether they want to use a condom or not and still remain protected.
.
Its thought, and still the subject of research, that even sexually active people who have not been vaccinated can still benefit from receiving the vaccine as it’s believed to offer some protection.

John: Is there a way of encouraging people to come forward so that early detection is possible. So for example if somebody recognizes that perhaps they have had a misspent period in their life, would it be worthwhile coming forward and saying I would like to be screened.
Dr. Torres-Holmes: Unlike cervical cancer, there is no good screening test for oropharyngeal cancer. You know you can do a pap smear for the cervix and asses risk. Unfortunately with oropharynx it is not the case. For patients any time they have a sore throat or neck lump that doesn’t go away within a month, that warrants investigation.

Dentists too should be on the look out for any abnormalities. At this stage men are three times more likely to develop oropharyngeal cancers than women. For Dr wetter the vaccine holds the key to putting the brakes on the rise of these cancers.

Dr. Wetter: It will increase until the children that have been vaccinated in early childhood or late childhood, early adolescence are becoming immune to the disease and eventually they no longer carry the HPV virus within their DNA.


PROMO 1

Smoking and Alcohol are no longer the only risk factors associated with contracting oropharyngeal cancer. An alarming rise in cases is now being linked to HPV, a sexually transmitted disease.

Dr. Torres: About 50% of all the cancers we see are HPV related


PROMO 2

Whilst smoking numbers are down, oral cancers are increasing. We look at why a common sexually transmitted disease, HPV, is now thought to be reason behind this surge.

Dr Torres: What’s really scary is that it is the only cancer, which is on the rise.


PROMO 3

Human Papillomavirus is well known for its connection to cervical cancer, now a rising case of oropharyngeal cancers are being linked to the common STD


Through condoms and commercially available devices targeting male to female oral sex

Safer oral sex through commercially available devices
